e05ec3e8d4.q: How does Arize use OpenTelemetry for AI agent observability?
e05ec3e8d4.a: All solutions around agent observability at Arize revolve around open telemetry. OpenTelemetry comes from traditionally the DevOps world, and while it comes with some overhead, it is the most common ground through which agents are able to observe data. Teams are already onboarded to OTEL, making it a huge unlock for agents because there are many unknown unknowns in agents on top of DevOps. OTEL has been a really good medium and the right way of thinking of things as they scale up.

aeee54f852.q: What is the difference between Open Telemetry semantics and OpenInference semantics for AI observability?
aeee54f852.a: OpenTelemetry is a general idea that applications have three primary signals: tracing (hierarchical interactions composed of spans that chain across network boundaries), structured logging, and metrics through Prometheus. f485282e3c.q: How should teams approach starting with evaluations for AI agents?
f485282e3c.a: You don't have to start with evals—it depends on how critical what you're building is. Evaluations work like layers of Swiss cheese with different layers and levels, and none of them will be perfect, but you want to guarantee that as the frontier shifts or model decisions change your system continues working. Evaluations can be a way to sift through data and don't always have to be perfect signals; people will use your platform in ways you didn't anticipate, so you can use LLM power to classify intent, segment data by region, or detect changing language patterns.

0d23b7f169.q: What security challenges does Arize face when open sourcing AI agent observability?
0d23b7f169.a: Cybersecurity is a particularly tough challenge. With closed source projects, it's harder to identify multi-vector attacks, but with open source it's much more likely attackers can figure out those attacks. The biggest current crack is that foundation model providers route cyber offensive capabilities to fallback models, making it impossible for even financially-backed open source projects to use frontier-class models' cyber expertise. This forces consideration of open-weight models for cyber defensive capabilities because attackers' capabilities are extremely emergent right now.

61513ad271.a: Pull requests used to be valuable for their code, but now the idea is what matters most.
